newsitem.title: UK: Change in Euro insurance sales exaggerated - report.
newsitem.headline: Change in Euro insurance sales exaggerated - report.

text.p: Modern methods of selling insurance, such as telephone sales and bancassurance, are making inroads in Europe but do not yet pose a threat to traditional distribution channels, a report said on Monday.

"'Traditional' channels such as tied agents, brokers and company employees continue to account for virtually all general insurance distribution in Europe," managament consultancy Datamonitor said in its report 'European General Insurance Distribution.'

It forecast that traditional channels would account for $316 billion out of a total of $384.5 billion in general insurance premiums in Europe in 2000, adding that the demise of the intermediary in Europe had been somewhat exaggerated.

"The value of direct distribution channels by the beginning of the 21st century is forecast to be $35.4 billion, most of it attributable to telephone sales. The value of banking channels...is expected to be in the region of $33.1 billion," Datamonitor said.

Ireland, the Netherlands, Sweden and the UK have seen the greatest advances by direct insurers, while in Denmark and Greece bancassurance has taken a strong hold, partly because banks own many insurance companies.
In other European countries, the new distribution channels may be slower to displace traditional methods, but their advent is encouraging rationalisation.

Belgium, Denmark, Germany and Portugal are set to see substantial shifts in distribution patterns, while others, such as Austria, Switzerland and Finland, will see very little meaningful change, the report said.
"Reinforcing tried and tested distribution strategies may prove, for many insurers, to be not only the safer option but also the wiser option," said Datamonitor analyst Riyaz Jivanjee.
